source_title: Slope traversal controls for planetary exploration rover on sandy terrain (Ishigami et al.; Journal of Field Robotics 26(3), 2009)
soil: Toyoura sand (dry, cohesionless laboratory quartz sand)
location: laboratory, Japan (sand box for slope traversal tests, 8.0 cm deep)
test_conditions: parameters used for the wheel force simulations of Figure 4 with wheel load 29.8 N, wheel radius 0.055 m, width 0.064 m
how_obtained: not stated in this paper (listed as the soil parameters used for the simulation, with the test soil assumed to be Toyoura sand)
notes: Units of kc and kphi are not printed, so the pressure sinkage form (Bekker or Reece dimensionless) cannot be confirmed from this paper. A 2016 thesis (Carletti, Table 1, research/sources/phase3/2016_12_Carletti.pdf) reproduces this set citing Ishigami but prints kphi0 = 120.54 (dimensionless), a factor of ten below 1,203.54, with Xc 26.0 deg, a0 0.4, a1 0.15; that copy is a secondary citation and is not used as a separate row. Verify against Ishigami's primary measurement report before use.

source_title: Terramechanics-based model for steering maneuver of planetary exploration rovers on loose soil (Ishigami et al.; Journal of Field Robotics 24(3), 2007)
soil: lunar regolith simulant equivalent to FJS-1 (loose, dry)
location: laboratory single wheel test bed, 12 cm deep vessel
test_conditions: single wheel 0.18 m diameter, 0.11 m wide, 10 mm paddles, load about 6.6 kg, slip 0 to 0.8, slip angle 5 to 30 deg
how_obtained: c and phi from shear strength test, kc kphi n from pressure sinkage test (Bekker 1960); lambda estimated visually; kx and ky empirical functions of slip angle beta (Sec 3.1)
slip_sinkage_or_other_coefficients: a0 0.40; a1 0.15; soil destructive angle Xc 26.4 deg; wheel sinkage ratio lambda 0.90 to 1.10
notes: Crushed volcanic lunar simulant with some cohesion, not quartz sand; the brief expected Toyoura sand here but this paper's Table I is for the FJS-1 equivalent simulant. Paired drawbar pull data: curve ishigami2007_fig11_slipangle5_fjs1.

source_title: Analysis of Angle of Attack for Efficient Slope Ascent by Rovers (H. Inotsume, Master's thesis, 2016)
location: laboratory single wheel rig and SLOPE tilt bed (NASA Glenn)
test_conditions: single wheel radius 0.16 m, width 0.15 m, weight 66.2 N; parameters used for the slope ascent model
how_obtained: c, phi, n and the fixed k_sigma and k adopted from Oravec et al. (thesis ref. 43, a secondary source); slip dependent k_sigma and k tuned in this thesis to single wheel tests
slip_sinkage_or_other_coefficients: k_sigma = c kc + rho g b kphi (Reece form, Eq. 2.18): fixed 4.20 x 10^5 N/m2; tuned 2.35 exp(-2.65 s) x 10^5 N/m2 (Eq. 2.32), s = slip ratio
notes: Table 2.1 cohesion is printed as < 1 kPa while Table 2.2 uses 500 Pa. The slip dependent k_sigma and k are the only values identified in this work. Paired slope curve: inotsume2016_fig3_9_scarab_direct_ascent (same simulant, different wheel).

source_title: Modeling of the interaction of rigid wheels with dry granular media (Agarwal et al.; Journal of Terramechanics 2019; arXiv 1901.10667)
soil: Quikrete 1962 Medium Sand (silica, 0.3 to 0.8 mm per evidence row TM-001)
test_conditions: loosely packed dry bed; forced slip single wheel rig, loads 80 to 190 N
how_obtained: plate penetration tests and direct shear tests (Table 1 caption); RFT constant extrapolated from plate tests
slip_sinkage_or_other_coefficients: RFT constant 2.02 N/cm3; packing fraction 0.6; MPM internal friction 0.53
notes: Negative kc and very large kphi as printed; flagged as unusual in evidence row TM-001. A fit with negative kc cannot be used outside the plate sizes tested. Same source as evidence rows TM-001 and TM-002 (different finding: parameter set).

source_title: Modeling of the interaction of rigid wheels with dry granular media (Agarwal et al.; Journal of Terramechanics 2019; arXiv 1901.10667)
soil: Mars Mojave Simulant (MMS), particles from micron to millimetre scale, 80 percent above 10 micron
test_conditions: dry bed; forced slip single wheel rig
how_obtained: plate penetration tests and direct shear tests (Table 1 caption); RFT constant extrapolated from plate tests
slip_sinkage_or_other_coefficients: RFT constant 3.05 N/cm3; packing fraction 0.6; MPM internal friction 0.50
notes: Mojave Desert derived Mars simulant with fines; not a well sorted dune sand.

source_title: Advance Simulation Method for Wheel-Terrain Interactions of Space Rovers: A Case Study on the UAE Rashid Rover (Abubakar et al.; arXiv 2308.12431, 2023)
soil: regolith simulant sample supplied by MBRSC (very loose, chosen to represent Lacus Somniorum)
test_conditions: Grouser Rashid rover wheel, wheel speed 3 cm/s, slip 0 to 0.75
how_obtained: soil properties collected from MBRSC (Sec IV); method not described
slip_sinkage_or_other_coefficients: weight density 13734 N/m3; d_gamma 0.1 gamma; eta 1.15; hb 0.01 m; Cf 800 Ns/m; kg' 0.06 (grouser oscillation model of Irani et al.)
notes: Paper reports that simulation with these values did not match the experiment (drawbar pull 10.2 N measured vs 6.2 N simulated).

source_title: Advance Simulation Method for Wheel-Terrain Interactions of Space Rovers: A Case Study on the UAE Rashid Rover (Abubakar et al.; arXiv 2308.12431, 2023)
soil: regolith simulant sample supplied by MBRSC (very loose, chosen to represent Lacus Somniorum)
test_conditions: tuned to the 0.25 slip single wheel test (configuration C2)
how_obtained: fine tuned to match single wheel experiment
slip_sinkage_or_other_coefficients: weight density 15620 N/m3; d_gamma 0.1 gamma; eta 1.15; hb 0.01 m; Cf 800 Ns/m; kg' 0.07; k0' 0.035
notes: Tuned values, not measurements; UAE relevant (Rashid rover) but lunar simulant.

source_title: Using high-fidelity discrete element simulation to calibrate an expeditious terramechanics model in a multibody dynamics framework (Zhang et al.; arXiv 2407.18903, 2024)
soil: DEM granular terrain (spherical particles, particle density 2650 kg/m3)
test_conditions: virtual plate sinkage and annulus shear tests in DEM
how_obtained: Bayesian calibration of SCM parameters against DEM virtual bevameter data
notes: Simulation only: parameters describe a virtual DEM material, not a measured sand; negative kc as printed.

source_title: Traction Performance Evaluation for a Rashid-1 Rover Wheel (Hurrell et al.; Space Science Reviews 221:37, 2025)
test_conditions: loose packing about 25 percent relative density; testbed bulk density 1410 to 1440 kg/m3
how_obtained: sieving; JIS A 1109 and JIS A 1224 for densities; fixed funnel angle of repose (six repeats); cohesion taken from Ozaki et al. (2023) as marked in the table
c_kPa: 0.9 (marked as measured in Ozaki et al. 2023)
phi_deg: not reported (angle of repose 34.3 plus or minus 0.8)
slip_sinkage_or_other_coefficients: particle density 2650 kg/m3; min bulk density 1369; max bulk density 1658 kg/m3
notes: Soil property set, not a Bekker parameter set; included because it is the measured state of the sand behind curves hurrell2025_fig5a and fig6a. Same sand family as ishigami2009_toyoura (rho 1490 there).
